newsitem.title: GERMANY: HAMBURG PORT TURNOVER UP IN FIRST HALF 1997.
newsitem.headline: HAMBURG PORT TURNOVER UP IN FIRST HALF 1997.

text.p: Turnover at the port of Hamburg in the first six months of 1997 was up by 7.3 percent from the same 1996 period at 37.61 million tonnes, the port promotion office said.
Container traffic increased by 8.1 percent to 19.65 million tonnes, especially with Asia, the office said ahead of a detailed report on first half activities later on this month.
The combined total of other categories, including suction, grab goods, liquid and general cargo accounted for the remainder of the total.
Grain export volumes had been down on Jan-June 1996 because export subsidies had been restricted, a source at the office said.
Public grain stocks for export had been reduced sharply by the middle of 1996, and were not replaced, he added.
Animal feeds imports had also been much reduced in first half 1997, with the exception of soybeans.
Port silo operators were hoping that grain exports may pick up again once the EU decides to market 1997/98 season grain.
While they were hopeful of marketing surpluses in the Middle East and North Africa, they were aware of competition from eastern Europe.
Ukraine, for example, may harvest up to 40 million tonnes, 60 percent more than last year, and export more than three million.

Fertiliser and scrap exports were up in the first six months while crude oil imports were down amid stangant consumption, the port also reported. A trend towards higher mineral oil product imports started in 1995 was still continuing.
